name: Power of a point
formula: PA \cdot PB = PC \cdot PD \qquad\text{and, for a tangent } PT,\quad PT^2 = PA \cdot PB
whenToUse: Two lines through the same point $P$ each meet a circle twice, or one line is tangent, and a length along one of the lines is unknown.
example: Chords $AB$ and $CD$ cross at $P$ inside a circle with $PA = 4$, $PB = 9$ and $PC = 6$. Then $6 \cdot PD = 4 \cdot 9 = 36$, so $PD = 6$.
pitfall: Every length is measured FROM $P$. For a secant from an outside point use the whole distance $P$ to the far intersection, not the length of the chord inside the circle.
derivation: Triangles $PAC$ and $PDB$ are similar because inscribed angles on the same arc are equal, so $PA/PD = PC/PB$, which rearranges to $PA \cdot PB = PC \cdot PD$.
